A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their readable main text, equations, figures and Appendices A–L support comparison. The NeurIPS checklist present in v1 is removed in v2.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendices K–L report original synthetic optimization experiments, Sentiment140 AUC results, TREC hyperparameter optimization results and empirical gradient-noise measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains the original synthetic, Sentiment140 and TREC experiments, hyperparameter sensitivity results and appendix gradient-noise measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 and the practical AUC variant retain their procedures. Equation (4) replaces separate base learning rates with a shared eta explicitly for analytical simplicity; this does not establish a changed algorithm or implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic minimax problem with noise levels 0, 20, 50 and 100, imbalanced Sentiment140 AUC maximization, and TREC hyperparameter optimization. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain TiAda for the synthetic experiment, SGDA/PDSM/TiAda for AUC maximization, and TFBO for bilevel optimization. New Tables 1–2 compare theoretical guarantees rather than introduce additional experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The reported architectures, metrics, training budgets, selected hyperparameters and testing procedures are retained. Appendix J replaces an enumerated learning-rate grid with its endpoint range; this reduces documentation specificity without establishing a different search protocol.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 retains the same sensitivity analyses for alpha, eta_x, eta_y and gamma. Appendix L retains the same empirical check of gradient-noise bounds. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: V1's checklist explicitly states that experiments were run once because of limited computational resources. V2 removes this disclosure with the checklist. Neither version reports experimental error bars or significance tests, and no increase in runs is established.

E6.justification: Figures 1–4 retain identical plot content and reported empirical findings. Appendix L retains the maximum and minimum noise measurements of 210.71 and 0.21. No empirical result entries are added, removed or numerically revised.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.3(i) adds an explicit bound on the stochastic gradient of F. Lemma E.3 corrects its hypergradient-noise bound to match the existing derivation, and Theorem 4.1 refines its stochastic-term coefficient. Definitions and lemma applicability are clarified across the appendices, while convergence orders and the main proof framework remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: noise-adaptive algorithms and sharp convergence guarantees for the same minimax and bilevel problem classes, supported by the same claimed empirical advantages.

C2.justification: V2 explains why the added stochastic-gradient bound is needed for Lemma E.3 and why equal base learning rates are only an analytical convenience. Section 6.2 additionally states that the existing fixed-horizon stepsize modification preserves convergence. The principal noise-lower-bound limitation remains.

D1.justification: Section 6 adds an explicit public code-repository pointer, whereas v1 only states in its checklist that code and data accompany supplementary material. Appendix J loses the exact learning-rate candidate list, retaining only the range [0.001, 0.1] and the same selected values.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Shen and Chen (2023), Lu (2023), and Lu and Mei (2024). Tables 1–2 make comparisons with TiAda and S-TFBO explicit through assumptions, settings and theoretical rates. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized explanatory and notation edits, reorganizes appendix theorem restatements and constant definitions, and removes the NeurIPS checklist. The main section sequence and overall scientific narrative are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds two theoretical comparison tables, places Algorithms 1–2 side by side, reformats theorem displays and relocates Figure 1 within the experimental discussion. The four empirical figures retain their plot content.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves mathematical consistency by explicitly stating the stochastic-gradient bound used in Lemma E.3 and correcting that lemma's noise-bound definition to match its proof. The comparison tables and code pointer also aid readers. These gains are tempered by loss of the single-run disclosure and exact tuning grid; the empirical evidence itself is unchanged.
